title: Paper 5 derivation output (Definitions 1-3)
description: derive.py's output: the minimal participation set P* (Definition 2) and the derived coverage list (Definition 3, the declared residue), plus enough provenance to reproduce and machine-check the run. One file per derivation run; checkers/participation_check.py reads this alongside pair-test-grid.yaml and loss-model.yaml to verify soundness and minimality exhaustively.

loss_model_sha256.description: sha256 of prereg/loss-model.yaml's bytes at derivation time -- freshness stamp, same inputs_hash pattern as checkers/_provenance.py.

grid_sha256.description: sha256 of prereg/pair-test-grid.yaml's bytes at derivation time.

candidate_properties.description: Every property Definition 1 was swept over -- the union of participating_properties and coverage_list; always equal to pair-test-grid.yaml's twelve declared rows.

participating_properties.description: P* (Definition 2): properties for which at least one witness pair exists. Sorted, deduplicated.

coverage_list.description: Definition 3: candidate_properties minus participating_properties -- the derived residue emitted honestly rather than silently dropped.

witnesses.description: For each participating property, at least one witness pair (a, a') from the executable-reachable set differing only in that property, with the loss id whose verdict differs between them -- the evidence a human or checker can replay without re-running the sweep.

grid_size_reachable.description: Count of executable-reachable tuples actually enumerated (post reachability filtering, rank-0 union remediation-reachable) -- a generated number, reported here so no paper claim of exhaustiveness can go unverified against it.

generated_at_head_sha.description: git HEAD at generation time -- informational, per checkers/_provenance.py's own head_sha()/inputs_hash() distinction (freshness is defined by the two *_sha256 fields above, not this one).
